subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which direct-invoke surfaces beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK, skill-dispatch, and command-cron paths should core support, and what owner/security gates are required for each?
rationale: The remaining work changes high-power tool execution boundaries and cannot be safely reduced to an autonomous bug fix without maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Keep the umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Track the broad request here while reviewing read/write/edit/readiness PRs as separate security-gated increments with explicit operator opt-ins.

options.title: Limit scope to shipped direct-invoke paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK, skill command dispatch, and command cron sufficient for core, then close or redirect broader CLI/chat/tool-call ideas to plugins or future proposals.

options.title: Approve a broader execution surface
options.body: Allow a larger CLI/chat/cron tool-call surface only after maintainers approve the trust model, dangerous-tool policy, and upgrade story.

recommendation.title: Keep the umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Track the broad request here while reviewing read/write/edit/readiness PRs as separate security-gated increments with explicit operator opt-ins.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged RPC direct-invoke path that current main builds on, making them the strongest history-linked owner for the remaining core boundary choice.
